record.statement: For synchronously coupled reflected Brownian motions in the exterior of a nondegenerate closed disk, can their distance have positive limsup with positive probability?
record.statement_caveat: This unbounded exterior geometry differs from the bounded-domain existence question.
record.title: Synchronous reflection outside a disk

record.independent_check: Both test locations lie in the exterior and the normal points into that same domain, fixing the otherwise easy sign error.
record.method: Exterior-disk reflection has both distance signs
record.obstruction: A global monotone-distance proof is unavailable. The question turns on boundary occupation and angular correlations over indefinitely long times.
record.result: At x=(R,0) on the inner circular boundary of the exterior domain, its inward-to-domain normal is (1,0). For y=(r,0), r>R, <x-y,n>=R-r<0; for y=(-r,0) it is R+r>0. Hence a reflection at X can either shrink or enlarge the synchronous separation.
